gmail.name: Modify email labels
gmail.description: Adds and/or removes specified Gmail labels for a message; ensure `message_id` and all `label_ids` are valid (use 'listLabels' for custom label IDs).

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you are accessing. Use 'me' if you want to access your own mailbox.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: Immutable ID of the message to modify. Gmail message IDs are hexadecimal strings (e.g., '1a2b3c4d5e6f7890'). IMPORTANT: Do NOT use UUIDs (32-character strings like '093ca4662b214d5eba8f4ceeaad63433'), thread IDs, or internal system IDs - these will cause 'Invalid id value' errors. Obtain valid message IDs from: (1) 'GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS' response 'messageId' field, (2) 'GMAIL_FETCH_MESSAGE_BY_THREAD_ID' response, or (3) 'GMAIL_LIST_THREADS' and then fetching thread messages.
message_id.human_parameter_description: Enter the Gmail message ID (a hexadecimal string like '1a2b3c4d5e6f7890'). Get this from GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS 'messageId' field. Do NOT use UUIDs or 32-character strings.

add_label_ids.title: Add Label Ids
add_label_ids.description: Label IDs to add (IDs, not display names). System labels: INBOX, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD, STARRED, IMPORTANT, CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES, CATEGORY_FORUMS. Use full CATEGORY_ prefix (e.g., 'CATEGORY_UPDATES' not 'UPDATES'). Custom labels: call 'listLabels' first to get the ID (format: 'Label_<number>'). Do NOT use the label display name; the API requires the ID. SENT, DRAFT, CHAT are immutable and cannot be added or removed. A label cannot appear in both add_label_ids and remove_label_ids.
add_label_ids.human_parameter_description: List the IDs of labels to add. Use exact system label IDs (e.g., 'CATEGORY_UPDATES' not 'UPDATES') or custom label IDs from listLabels (e.g., 'Label_1' not the label name). Note: SENT, DRAFT, and CHAT cannot be modified.

remove_label_ids.title: Remove Label Ids
remove_label_ids.description: Label IDs to remove (IDs, not display names). System labels: INBOX, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD, STARRED, IMPORTANT, CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES, CATEGORY_FORUMS. Use full CATEGORY_ prefix (e.g., 'CATEGORY_UPDATES' not 'UPDATES'). Custom labels: call 'listLabels' first to get the ID (format: 'Label_<number>'). SENT, DRAFT, CHAT are immutable and cannot be removed. Common operations: to mark as read, remove 'UNREAD'; to archive, remove 'INBOX'. A label cannot appear in both add_label_ids and remove_label_ids.
remove_label_ids.human_parameter_description: List the IDs of labels to remove. Use exact system label IDs (e.g., 'CATEGORY_UPDATES' not 'UPDATES') or custom label IDs from listLabels (e.g., 'Label_1' not the label name). To mark as read, remove 'UNREAD'. To archive, remove 'INBOX'. Note: SENT, DRAFT, and CHAT cannot be modified.

gmail.name: Batch delete Gmail messages
gmail.description: Permanently deletes multiple Gmail messages by ID, bypassing Trash. A successful request does not confirm individual messages existed or were deleted.

input_parameters.title: BatchDeleteMessagesRequest

userId.title: User Id
userId.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.
userId.human_parameter_description: The email address of the user whose messages you want to delete. Use 'me' to apply changes to your own account.

messageIds.title: Message Ids
messageIds.description: List of Gmail message IDs to delete. Each ID must be a hexadecimal string (e.g., '18c5f5d1a2b3c4d5'). Obtain IDs from actions like GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS or GMAIL_LIST_THREADS - do not use human-readable descriptions.
messageIds.human_parameter_description: The unique message IDs for the emails you wish to delete. Each ID is a hexadecimal string (like '18c5f5d1a2b3c4d5'). Get these IDs by first fetching or listing messages.

input_parameters.description: Request model for bulk deletion of Gmail messages by ID.

gmail.name: Batch modify Gmail messages
gmail.description: Adds or removes labels on up to 1,000 Gmail messages in one request, supporting operations such as archiving and marking messages read or unread. A successful response confirms request acceptance, not individual message status.

userId.title: User Id
userId.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.
userId.human_parameter_description: Indicate which user's mailbox you are trying to modify. Use 'me' for your own mailbox or provide a specific email address.

messageIds.title: Message Ids
messageIds.description: List of message IDs to modify. Maximum 1,000 message IDs per request. Get message IDs from GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS or GMAIL_LIST_THREADS actions. Accepts 'messageIds', 'ids', or 'message_ids' as the parameter name.
messageIds.human_parameter_description: Provide the unique IDs of the messages you want to modify. You can collect these IDs from previous email fetch or list actions.

addLabelIds.title: Add Label Ids
addLabelIds.description: List of label IDs to add to the messages. IMPORTANT: Use label IDs, NOT label display names. System labels use their name as ID: INBOX, STARRED, IMPORTANT, SENT, DRAFT, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD, CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES, CATEGORY_FORUMS. Custom labels MUST use their ID (format: 'Label_XXX', e.g., 'Label_1', 'Label_25'), NOT the display name (e.g., do NOT use 'Work' or 'Projects'). Call GMAIL_LIST_LABELS first to get the 'id' field for custom labels. At least one of add_label_ids or remove_label_ids must be provided. CONSTRAINT: Label IDs must NOT overlap with remove_label_ids - cannot add and remove the same label.
addLabelIds.human_parameter_description: Specify the label IDs you want to add. For system labels use INBOX, STARRED, etc. For custom labels, first call GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to get the label ID (format: Label_XXX).

removeLabelIds.title: Remove Label Ids
removeLabelIds.description: List of label IDs to remove from the messages. IMPORTANT: Use label IDs, NOT label display names. System labels use their name as ID: INBOX, STARRED, IMPORTANT, SENT, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD. Custom labels MUST use their ID (format: 'Label_XXX', e.g., 'Label_1', 'Label_25'), NOT the display name (e.g., do NOT use 'Work' or 'Projects'). Call GMAIL_LIST_LABELS first to get the 'id' field for custom labels. Common use cases: Remove 'UNREAD' to mark as read, remove 'INBOX' to archive. Note: 'DRAFT' cannot be removed - use GMAIL_DELETE_DRAFT instead. At least one of add_label_ids or remove_label_ids must be provided. CONSTRAINT: Label IDs must NOT overlap with add_label_ids - cannot add and remove the same label.
removeLabelIds.human_parameter_description: Specify the label IDs you want to remove. For system labels use INBOX, UNREAD, etc. For custom labels, first call GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to get the label ID (format: Label_XXX). Note: DRAFT cannot be removed - use GMAIL_DELETE_DRAFT instead.

gmail.name: Create email draft
gmail.description: Creates a Gmail draft with optional recipients, subject, plain or HTML body, attachments, and threading. When a requested thread cannot be fetched, the draft is created without threading; a provided subject is used instead of the thread subject.

cc.title: Cc
cc.description: Carbon Copy (CC) recipients' email addresses. Each must be a valid email address (e.g., 'user@example.com') or display name format (e.g., 'John Doe <user@example.com>'). Plain names without email addresses are NOT valid. Optional for drafts (recipients can be added later before sending).

bcc.title: Bcc
bcc.description: Blind Carbon Copy (BCC) recipients' email addresses. Each must be a valid email address (e.g., 'user@example.com') or display name format (e.g., 'Bob Jones <user@example.com>'). Plain names without email addresses are NOT valid. Optional for drafts (recipients can be added later before sending).

body.title: Body
examples:
Hello Team,

Please find the attached report for your review.

Best regards,
Your Name

Meeting Confirmation

This email confirms our meeting scheduled for next Tuesday.
body.description: Email body content (plain text or HTML); `is_html` must be True if HTML. Optional - drafts can be created without a body and edited later before sending. Can also be provided as 'message_body'.
body.human_parameter_description: Write the main content of your email here. This can be plain text or HTML, depending on your preference.

is_html.title: Is Html
is_html.description:
Set to True if `body` is already formatted HTML. When False, plain text newlines are auto-converted to
tags. Both modes result in HTML email; this flag controls whether the body content is treated as raw HTML or plain text that gets HTML formatting applied.
is_html.human_parameter_description: Set to True if your email body is already HTML. When False, plain text formatting (newlines, tabs) will be automatically converted to HTML for proper display.

subject.title: Subject
subject.description: Email subject line. Optional - drafts can be created without a subject and edited later before sending. When creating a draft reply to an existing thread (thread_id provided), leave this empty to stay in the same thread. Setting a subject will create a NEW thread instead.
subject.human_parameter_description: Enter the subject of your email. This helps the recipient understand what the email is about.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the user ID or the email address of the user. Use 'me' to refer to the currently authenticated user.

thread_id.title: Thread Id
thread_id.description: ID of an existing Gmail thread to reply to; omit for new thread. If the thread ID is invalid or inaccessible, the draft will be created as a new thread instead of failing.
thread_id.human_parameter_description: If you want to reply to an ongoing conversation, provide the thread ID here. Leave it blank for a new message.

name.title: Name
name.description: The filename that will be used when uploading the file to the destination service

s3key.title: S3Key
s3key.description: The S3 key of a publicly accessible file, typically returned from a previous download action that stored the file in S3. This key references an existing file that can be uploaded to another service.

mimetype.title: Mimetype
mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file

s3key.description: The S3 key of a publicly accessible file, typically returned from a previous download action that stored the file in S3. This key references an existing file that can be uploaded to another service.

mimetype.description: The MIME type of the file

attachment.title: Attachment
attachment.description: File(s) to attach to the email. Accepts a single file or a list of files. Total message size including base64-encoded attachments must be under 25 MB; use shareable links (e.g., Google Drive) for larger files.
attachment.human_parameter_description: Upload file(s) you want to include with the email. Can be a single file or multiple files.

recipient_email.title: Recipient Email
recipient_email.description: Primary recipient's email address. Must be a valid email address (e.g., 'user@example.com') or display name format (e.g., 'John Doe <user@example.com>'). A plain name without an email address (e.g., 'John Doe') is NOT valid - the '@' symbol and domain are required. Optional for drafts (recipients can be added later before sending). Use extra_recipients if you want to send to multiple recipients.

extra_recipients.title: Extra Recipients
extra_recipients.description: Additional 'To' recipients' email addresses (not Cc or Bcc). Each must be a valid email address (e.g., 'user@example.com'), display name format (e.g., 'Jane Doe <user@example.com>'), or 'me' for the authenticated user. Plain names without email addresses are NOT valid. Should only be used if recipient_email is also provided.

include_signature.title: Include Signature
include_signature.description: Append the sender's Gmail signature (the 'Send mail as' signature configured in Gmail settings) to the message body, ahead of any quoted or forwarded content. Skipped when the body already ends with that signature, when no signature is configured, or when the connection lacks permission to read Gmail settings. Set to false to send the body exactly as provided.
include_signature.human_parameter_description: Append the sender's configured Gmail signature to the message.

gmail.description: Tool to create a new Gmail filter with specified criteria and actions. Use when the user wants to automatically organize incoming messages based on sender, subject, size, or other criteria. Note: you can only create a maximum of 1,000 filters per account.

action.title: Action

forward.title: Forward
forward.description: Email address that the message should be forwarded to.

addLabelIds.title: Add Label Ids
addLabelIds.description: List of label IDs to add to the message.

removeLabelIds.title: Remove Label Ids
removeLabelIds.description: List of label IDs to remove from the message.

gmail.name: Create label
gmail.description: Creates a Gmail label and returns its label ID. For nested labels, it may create missing parent labels; on a name conflict it attempts to return the existing matching label.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The email address of the user in whose account the label will be created.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the email address or identifier of the user for whom you want to create a label. Use 'me' to refer to your own account.

label_name.title: Label Name
label_name.description: REQUIRED. The name for the new label. Must be unique within the account, non-blank, maximum length 225 characters, cannot contain commas (','), not only whitespace, and must not be a reserved system label. Reserved English system labels include: Inbox, Starred, Important, Sent, Draft, Drafts, Spam, Trash, etc. Forward slashes ('/') are allowed and used to create hierarchical nested labels (e.g., 'Work/Projects', 'Personal/Finance'). When creating nested labels, any missing parent labels will be automatically created (similar to 'mkdir -p'). Periods ('.') are allowed and commonly used for numbering schemes (e.g., '1. Action Items', '2. Projects'). Note: 'name' is also accepted as an alias for this field. If a label with this name already exists, returns a 409 conflict; use GMAIL_LIST_LABELS to check existing labels and reuse the existing labelId, or use GMAIL_PATCH_LABEL to update it.

text_color.title: GmailLabelColor
text_color.description: Text color for the label. Gmail only accepts colors from a predefined palette of 102 specific hex values. Common color names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN', 'ORANGE', 'PURPLE', 'PINK' are automatically mapped to the closest Gmail palette color. Provide either a common color name, a Gmail palette color name (e.g., 'BLACK', 'ROYAL_BLUE'), or exact hex value (e.g., '#000000', '#4a86e8'). If only text_color is provided without background_color, a complementary background color (white or black) will be auto-selected for optimal contrast. Full palette: https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.labels#Color Must be supplied together with background_color — providing only one will cause a 400 error. The auto-selected complementary color behavior does not apply; both colors are required.
text_color.human_parameter_description: Pick a color for the label text. Common names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN' are automatically mapped to Gmail palette colors.

background_color.title: GmailLabelColor
background_color.description: Background color for the label. Gmail only accepts colors from a predefined palette of 102 specific hex values. Common color names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN', 'ORANGE', 'PURPLE', 'PINK' are automatically mapped to the closest Gmail palette color. Provide either a common color name, a Gmail palette color name (e.g., 'ROYAL_BLUE', 'CARIBBEAN_GREEN'), or exact hex value (e.g., '#4a86e8', '#43d692'). If only background_color is provided without text_color, a complementary text color (white or black) will be auto-selected for optimal contrast. Full palette: https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.labels#Color Must be supplied together with text_color — providing only one will cause a 400 error. The auto-selected complementary color behavior does not apply; both colors are required.
background_color.human_parameter_description: Choose a background color for your label. Common names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN' are automatically mapped to Gmail palette colors.

label_list_visibility.title: Label List Visibility
label_list_visibility.description: Controls how the label is displayed in the label list in the Gmail sidebar. Valid values: 'labelShow' (always show), 'labelShowIfUnread' (show only if unread messages), 'labelHide' (hide from list).
label_list_visibility.human_parameter_description: Select how you want the label to appear in the Gmail sidebar. You can show it all the time, show it only if there are unread messages, or hide it completely.

message_list_visibility.title: Message List Visibility
message_list_visibility.description: Controls how messages with this label are displayed in the message list. Valid values: 'show' or 'hide'. Note: These values are different from label_list_visibility - do NOT use 'labelShow' or 'labelHide' here.
message_list_visibility.human_parameter_description: Choose whether messages with this label should be visible in the message list or hidden away.

gmail.name: Delete Draft
gmail.description: Permanently deletes a specific Gmail draft using its ID with no recovery possible; verify the correct `draft_id` and obtain explicit user confirmation before calling. Ensure the draft exists and the user has necessary permissions for the given `user_id`.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user; 'me' is recommended.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address of the user whose drafts you want to manage. Use 'me' to refer to the authenticated user.

draft_id.title: Draft Id
draft_id.description: Immutable ID of the draft to delete. Must be obtained from GMAIL_LIST_DRAFTS or GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT actions. Draft IDs typically have an 'r' prefix (e.g., 'r-1234567890' or 'r1234567890'). Draft IDs differ from message IDs used in GMAIL_BATCH_DELETE_MESSAGES — do not interchange. When multiple similar drafts exist, confirm the exact ID via GMAIL_LIST_DRAFTS before deleting.
draft_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier for the draft you wish to delete. Obtain this ID from listing drafts (GMAIL_LIST_DRAFTS) or when creating a draft (GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT).

gmail.name: Delete Gmail filter
gmail.description: Tool to permanently delete a Gmail filter by its ID. Use when you need to remove an existing email filtering rule.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.

filter_id.title: Filter Id
filter_id.description: The ID of the filter to be deleted. Filter IDs can be obtained from GMAIL_LIST_FILTERS action.

gmail.name: Delete label from account (permanent)
gmail.description: Permanently DELETES a user-created Gmail label from the account (not from a message). WARNING: This action DELETES the label definition itself, removing it from all messages. System labels (INBOX, SENT, UNREAD, etc.) cannot be deleted. To add/remove labels from specific messages, use GMAIL_ADD_LABEL_TO_EMAIL action instead.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address of the user whose labels you want to manage. Use 'me' if you're accessing your own labels.

label_id.title: Label Id
label_id.description: ID of the user-created label to be permanently DELETED from the account. Must be a custom label ID (format: 'Label_<id>' e.g., 'Label_1', 'Label_42'). System labels (INBOX, SENT, DRAFT, UNREAD, STARRED, IMPORTANT, SPAM, TRASH, CATEGORY_*, etc.) cannot be deleted. WARNING: This action permanently DELETES the label definition from your account - it does NOT remove a label from a message. To add/remove labels from messages, use GMAIL_ADD_LABEL_TO_EMAIL instead.
label_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the custom label you wish to permanently DELETE from your Gmail account. System labels cannot be deleted. To remove a label from a message (e.g., mark as read), use GMAIL_ADD_LABEL_TO_EMAIL instead.

gmail.name: Delete message
gmail.description: Permanently deletes a specific email message by its ID from a Gmail mailbox; for `user_id`, use 'me' for the authenticated user or an email address to which the authenticated user has delegated access.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address. The special value 'me' refers to the authenticated user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own mailbox.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: Identifier of the email message to delete.
message_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the email message you want to delete. You can find this ID from previous message searches or lists.

gmail.name: Delete thread

id.title: Id

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address. The special value 'me' refers to the authenticated user.

gmail.name: Fetch emails
gmail.description: Lists Gmail messages with query and label filtering, pagination, and optional message details. Individual detail fetches returning 404, 429, or 503 are skipped, so a page can contain fewer messages than the list result.

query.title: Query
query.description: Gmail advanced search query (e.g., 'from:user subject:meeting'). Supported operators: 'from:', 'to:', 'subject:', 'label:', 'has:', 'is:', 'in:', 'category:', 'after:YYYY/MM/DD', 'before:YYYY/MM/DD', AND/OR/NOT. IMPORTANT - 'is:' vs 'label:' usage: Use 'is:' for special mail states: is:snoozed, is:unread, is:read, is:starred, is:important. Use 'label:' ONLY for user-created labels (e.g., 'label:work', 'label:projects'). Note: 'muted' may work with both 'is:muted' and 'label:muted' based on community reports. Common mistake: 'label:snoozed' is WRONG - use 'is:snoozed' instead. Use quotes for exact phrases. Omit for no query filter. after:/before: evaluate whole calendar days in UTC; before: is exclusive — adjust for local timezone to avoid off-by-one-day gaps.
query.human_parameter_description: Input a search term to filter your emails. Use 'is:' for special states (is:snoozed, is:unread, is:read, is:starred, is:important). Use 'label:' only for user-created labels (exception: 'muted' may work with both).

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user. Non-'me' addresses require domain-level delegation; without it, authentication or not-found errors result.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the email address of the user whose mailbox you want to access. You can use 'me' to refer to your own mailbox.

verbose.title: Verbose
verbose.description: If false, uses optimized concurrent metadata fetching for faster performance (~75% improvement). If true, uses standard detailed message fetching. When false, only essential fields (subject, sender, recipient, time, labels) are guaranteed. Body content and attachment details require verbose=true even when include_payload=true.
verbose.human_parameter_description: Select this to get detailed information for each email or to speed up the process and get just the basics.

ids_only.title: Ids Only
ids_only.description: If true, only returns message IDs from the list API without fetching individual message details. Fastest option for getting just message IDs and thread IDs.
ids_only.human_parameter_description: Use this option if you just want the IDs of emails without loading their full details, making the request quicker.

label_ids.title: Label Ids
label_ids.description: Filter by label IDs; only messages with all specified labels are returned (AND logic). Optional - omit or use empty list to fetch all messages without label filtering. System label IDs: 'INBOX', 'SPAM', 'TRASH', 'UNREAD', 'STARRED', 'IMPORTANT', 'CATEGORY_PRIMARY' (alias 'CATEGORY_PERSONAL'), 'CATEGORY_SOCIAL', 'CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS', 'CATEGORY_UPDATES', 'CATEGORY_FORUMS'. For custom/user-created labels, you MUST use the label ID (e.g., 'Label_123456'), NOT the display name. Use the 'listLabels' action to find label IDs for custom labels. Combining label_ids with label: in query applies AND logic across both, which can silently over-restrict results; use one strategy consistently.
label_ids.human_parameter_description: List the label IDs to filter which messages to fetch. System labels (INBOX, SPAM, etc.) can be used directly by name. For custom labels, you must use the listLabels action first to get the label ID - do not use the label name you see in Gmail.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Token for retrieving a specific page, obtained from a previous response's `nextPageToken`. Must be a valid opaque token string from a previous API response. Do not pass arbitrary values. Omit for the first page. Loop calls using nextPageToken until it is absent to avoid silently missing messages. resultSizeEstimate is approximate — do not use as a stopping condition.
page_token.human_parameter_description: If you've paginated results, use this token to get the next set of messages. Leave blank for the first page.

max_results.title: Max Results
max_results.description: Maximum number of messages to retrieve per page. Default of 1 retrieves only a single message; set higher for practical use. Hard cap is 500 per page.
max_results.human_parameter_description: Specify how many email messages you want to retrieve in one request, from 1 to 500.

include_payload.title: Include Payload
include_payload.description: Set to true to include full message payload (headers, body, attachments); false for metadata only. payload may still be null even when true; use GMAIL_FETCH_MESSAGE_BY_MESSAGE_ID for guaranteed complete content. When payload is present, bodies are base64url-encoded in payload.parts; replace '-'→'+' and '_'→'/' and fix padding before decoding, and check both text/plain and text/html parts.
include_payload.human_parameter_description: Choose whether to get the full content of each email, including attachments and body, or just the essential metadata.

include_spam_trash.title: Include Spam Trash
include_spam_trash.description: Set to true to include messages from 'SPAM' and 'TRASH'.
include_spam_trash.human_parameter_description: Decide if you want to see emails that are normally filtered into your SPAM or TRASH folders.

gmail.name: Fetch message by message ID
gmail.description: Fetches a Gmail message by its message ID in the requested format and returns formatted message details. Available fields depend on the format.

format.title: Format
format.description: Format for message content. 'minimal': lightest (ID, thread ID, labels only). 'metadata': headers and message metadata without body content - ideal for summarization, analysis, or when you only need subject/sender/timestamp (recommended for most use cases). 'full': complete MIME structure with 50+ headers, nested parts, and base64url-encoded body data - heavy payload, only use when you need the complete raw MIME structure for parsing attachments or body content. 'raw': entire RFC 2822 formatted message as base64url string.
format.human_parameter_description: Choose the response format: 'metadata' for summarization/analysis (recommended), 'minimal' for just IDs/labels, 'full' only when you need complete MIME structure.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own mailbox.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: The Gmail API message ID (hexadecimal string, typically 15-16 characters like '19b11732c1b578fd'). Must be obtained from Gmail API responses (e.g., List Messages, Search Messages). Do NOT use email subjects, dates, sender names, or custom identifiers. Do NOT use `threadId` (use GMAIL_FETCH_MESSAGE_BY_THREAD_ID for threads), the Message-ID email header, or any fabricated value — only IDs from Gmail API list/search responses.
message_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the email message you want to fetch. You'll use this ID to tell the system which specific email to retrieve.

gmail.name: Fetch Message by Thread ID
gmail.description: Retrieves messages from an accessible Gmail thread by thread ID, returning thread details and a messages array. Message order is not guaranteed; use messageTimestamp to identify oldest or newest messages and labelIds to filter drafts.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The email address of the user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own mailbox.

thread_id.title: Thread Id
thread_id.description: Hexadecimal thread ID from Gmail API (e.g., '19bf77729bcb3a44'). Obtain from GMAIL_LIST_THREADS or GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS. Prefixes like 'msg-f:' or 'thread-f:' are auto-stripped. Legacy Gmail web UI IDs (e.g., 'FMfcgzQfBZdVqKZcSVBhqwWLKWCtDdWQ') are NOT supported - use the API thread ID instead. Deduplicate thread_ids before calling when multiple listed messages share the same threadId to avoid redundant calls.
thread_id.human_parameter_description: The unique hexadecimal identifier of the email thread (e.g., '19bf77729bcb3a44'). Obtain this from GMAIL_LIST_THREADS or GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS actions. Legacy Gmail web UI IDs are not supported.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Opaque page token for fetching a specific page of messages if results are paginated. Iterate calls by passing the returned `nextPageToken` until it is absent; stopping early will miss messages in long threads.
page_token.human_parameter_description: Use this token to navigate to a specific set of messages if there are many. It helps in paginating through results.

gmail.name: Forward email message
gmail.description: Forwards an existing Gmail message to specified recipients, with optional additional text. The tool copies original message parts into a new message, but may alter MIME structure and attachment metadata.

cc.title: Cc
cc.description: List of email addresses to CC.
cc.human_parameter_description: Email addresses to include in the CC (carbon copy) field. This is optional.

bcc.title: Bcc
bcc.description: List of email addresses to BCC.
bcc.human_parameter_description: Email addresses to include in the BCC (blind carbon copy) field. This is optional.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own mailbox.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: Gmail message ID (hexadecimal string, e.g., '17f45ec49a9c3f1b'). Must contain only hex characters [0-9a-fA-F]. Obtain this from actions like 'List Messages' or 'Fetch Emails'.
message_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the email message you want to forward. You can get this from a previous message search or list operation.

recipients.title: Recipients
recipients.description: List of email addresses to forward the message to.
recipients.human_parameter_description: The email addresses of the people you want to send the forwarded message to. Provide at least one email address.

additional_text.title: Additional Text
examples: Please see the forwarded message below.
additional_text.description: Optional additional text to include before the forwarded content.
additional_text.human_parameter_description: Any extra message you want to include before the forwarded email content. This is optional.

include_signature.title: Include Signature
include_signature.description: Append the sender's Gmail signature (the 'Send mail as' signature configured in Gmail settings) to the message body, ahead of any quoted or forwarded content. Skipped when the body already ends with that signature, when no signature is configured, or when the connection lacks permission to read Gmail settings. Set to false to send the body exactly as provided.
include_signature.human_parameter_description: Append the sender's configured Gmail signature to the message.

gmail.name: Get Gmail attachment
gmail.description: Retrieves a Gmail message attachment by message and attachment IDs and returns a downloadable file using the supplied filename.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's email address ('me' for authenticated user).
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own mailbox.

file_name.title: File Name
file_name.description: Desired filename for the downloaded attachment. This is a required string field - do not pass null.
file_name.human_parameter_description: The name you want to give the file once it's downloaded. This helps you easily identify the attachment later.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: Immutable ID of the message containing the attachment. This is a required string field - do not pass null. Obtain the message_id from Gmail API responses (e.g., fetchEmails, listThreads).
message_id.human_parameter_description: The unique identifier of the email message that contains the attachment you want to retrieve.

attachment_id.title: Attachment Id
attachment_id.description: The internal Gmail attachment ID (NOT the filename). This is a system-generated token string like 'ANGjdJ8s...'. Obtain this ID from the 'attachmentId' field in the 'attachmentList' array returned by fetchEmails or fetchMessageByMessageId actions. Do NOT pass the filename (e.g., 'report.pdf'). Requires a fully hydrated message payload: call GMAIL_FETCH_MESSAGE_BY_MESSAGE_ID with format='full' to obtain valid attachment IDs — lightweight fetch modes may omit attachmentList entirely.
attachment_id.human_parameter_description: The unique Gmail attachment ID token (NOT the filename). This is a system-generated ID string obtained from the 'attachmentId' field in message attachment lists. First fetch the email using fetchEmails or fetchMessageByMessageId to get the attachmentId, then use it here.

gmail.name: Get Auto-Forwarding Settings
gmail.description: Tool to get the auto-forwarding setting for the specified account. Use when you need to retrieve the current auto-forwarding configuration including enabled status, forwarding email address, and message disposition.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

gmail.name: Get contacts
gmail.description: Lists saved Google contacts with selectable fields and pagination, optionally including Other Contacts. Other Contacts are fetched on the first page; endpoint failures can result in partial results, and contact records may be sparse.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Token to retrieve a specific page of results, obtained from 'nextPageToken' in a previous response. Repeat calls with each successive `nextPageToken` until it is absent — stopping early silently omits contacts.
page_token.human_parameter_description: Use this token to fetch a specific page of results. It helps you navigate through large sets of contacts.

person_fields.title: Person Fields
person_fields.description: Comma-separated person fields to retrieve for each contact (e.g., 'names,emailAddresses').
person_fields.human_parameter_description: List the fields you want to get for each contact, separated by commas. This helps you customize the information returned.

resource_name.title: Resource Name
resource_name.description: Identifier for the person resource whose connections are listed; use 'people/me' for the authenticated user.
resource_name.human_parameter_description: Provide the identifier for the person's resource. Use 'people/me' to access your own account.

include_other_contacts.title: Include Other Contacts
include_other_contacts.description: Include 'Other Contacts' (interacted with but not explicitly saved) in addition to regular contacts. WARNING: 'Other Contacts' often have incomplete data - they may lack names, phone numbers, and other fields even when requested. These auto-generated contacts are created from email interactions and typically only have email addresses. Set to False if you need contacts with complete name information. When True, each contact will have a 'contactSource' field indicating its origin. When True, `person_fields` is restricted to `emailAddresses`, `names`, `phoneNumbers`, and `metadata` only — requesting other fields (e.g., `organizations`, `birthdays`) causes validation errors or silent omissions.
include_other_contacts.human_parameter_description: Decide whether to include contacts you've interacted with but haven't saved. WARNING: These contacts often only have email addresses and may lack names and other requested fields.

gmail.name: Get Draft
gmail.description: Retrieves a single Gmail draft by its ID. Use this to fetch and inspect draft content before sending via GMAIL_SEND_DRAFT. The format parameter controls the level of detail returned.

format.title: Format
format.description: Format for the draft message: 'minimal' (ID/labels only), 'full' (complete data with parsed payload), 'raw' (base64url-encoded RFC 2822 format), 'metadata' (ID/labels/headers only).

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address. The special value `me` can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

draft_id.title: Draft Id
draft_id.description: The ID of the draft to retrieve. Draft IDs are typically alphanumeric strings (e.g., 'r99885592323229922'). Use GMAIL_LIST_DRAFTS to retrieve valid draft IDs.

gmail.name: Get Gmail filter
gmail.description: Tool to retrieve a specific Gmail filter by its ID. Use when you need to inspect the criteria and actions of an existing filter.

id.title: Id
id.description: The ID of the filter to be fetched.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address or the special value 'me' to indicate the authenticated user.

gmail.name: Get label details
gmail.description: Gets details for a specified Gmail label. Use this to retrieve label information including name, type, visibility settings, message/thread counts, and color.

id.title: Id
id.description: The ID of the label to retrieve. Can be a system label (e.g., INBOX, SENT, DRAFT, UNREAD, STARRED, SPAM, TRASH) or a user-created label ID (e.g., Label_1, Label_42).

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

gmail.name: Get Language Settings
gmail.description: Tool to retrieve the language settings for a Gmail user. Use when you need to determine the display language preference for the authenticated user or a specific Gmail account.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The email address of the Gmail user whose language settings are to be retrieved, or the special value 'me' to indicate the currently authenticated user.

gmail.name: Get People
gmail.description: Retrieves a person's details by resource name or lists the authenticated user's Other Contacts, using a field mask to select the information returned. Other Contacts can be paginated and queried using a sync token for changes since a previous sync.

items.title: ReadSourceType
items.description: Source types for reading other contacts.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Source types to include when retrieving other contacts. READ_SOURCE_TYPE_CONTACT supports basic fields (emailAddresses, metadata, names, phoneNumbers, photos). READ_SOURCE_TYPE_PROFILE supports extended fields (birthdays, genders, organizations, etc.) but requires READ_SOURCE_TYPE_CONTACT to also be included. Applicable only when `other_contacts` is true.
sources.human_parameter_description: Choose which types of contact information to retrieve. Contact source provides basic info, while Profile source adds extended details.

page_size.title: Page Size
page_size.description: The number of 'Other Contacts' to return per page. Applicable only when `other_contacts` is true.
page_size.human_parameter_description: Indicate how many 'Other Contacts' you want to see in each response. You can choose between 1 and 1000.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: An opaque token from a previous response to retrieve the next page of 'Other Contacts' results. Applicable only when `other_contacts` is true and paginating.
page_token.human_parameter_description: Provide this token to continue fetching more contacts from where you left off.

sync_token.title: Sync Token
sync_token.description: A token from a previous 'Other Contacts' list call to retrieve only changes since the last sync; leave empty for an initial full sync. Applicable only when `other_contacts` is true.
sync_token.human_parameter_description: Use this token to get updates from your last sync, so you only see new changes.

person_fields.title: Person Fields
person_fields.description: A comma-separated field mask to restrict which fields on the person (or persons) are returned. Consult the Google People API documentation for a comprehensive list of valid fields. Omitted fields are silently absent from the response — no error is raised. When `other_contacts` is true, only a restricted subset is valid (`emailAddresses`, `names`, `phoneNumbers`, `metadata`); extended fields like `organizations` or `birthdays` may cause validation errors or silent omissions in that mode.
person_fields.human_parameter_description: Specify which details about the person you want to retrieve, such as their names or email addresses.

resource_name.title: Resource Name
resource_name.description: Resource name identifying the person for whom to retrieve information (like the authenticated user or a specific contact). Used only when `other_contacts` is false. Deleted or stale resource_names may return partial records with missing `emailAddresses`, `names`, or other fields.
resource_name.human_parameter_description: The identifier for the person whose information you want to retrieve. You can use 'people/me' to refer to yourself.

other_contacts.title: Other Contacts
other_contacts.description: If true, retrieves 'Other Contacts' (people interacted with but not explicitly saved), ignoring `resource_name` and enabling pagination/sync. If false, retrieves information for the single person specified by `resource_name`.
other_contacts.human_parameter_description: Choose whether you want to get a list of people you've interacted with or just details about a specific person.

gmail.name: Get Profile
gmail.description: Retrieves Gmail profile information (email address, aggregate messagesTotal/threadsTotal, historyId) for a user. messagesTotal counts individual emails; threadsTotal counts conversations; neither is per-label — use GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS with label filters for label-specific counts. The returned historyId seeds incremental sync via GMAIL_LIST_HISTORY; if historyIdTooOld is returned, rescan with GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS before resuming. Response may be wrapped under a top-level data field; unwrap before reading fields. A successful call confirms mailbox connectivity but not full mailbox access if granted scopes are narrow. Use the returned email address to dynamically identify the authenticated account rather than hard-coding it.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The email address of the Gmail user whose profile is to be retrieved, or the special value 'me' to indicate the currently authenticated user. Prefer 'me' unless explicitly targeting another account; passing a raw email address that does not match the connected account may fail or access the wrong mailbox.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the email address of the user whose profile you want to see. Use 'me' to view your own profile.

gmail.name: Get Vacation Settings
gmail.description: Tool to retrieve vacation responder settings for a Gmail user. Use when you need to check if out-of-office auto-replies are configured and view their content.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The email address of the Gmail user whose vacation settings are to be retrieved, or the special value 'me' to indicate the currently authenticated user.

gmail.name: Import message
gmail.description: Tool to import a message into the user's mailbox with standard email delivery scanning and classification. Use when you need to add an existing email to a Gmail account without sending it through SMTP. This method doesn't perform SPF checks, so it might not work for some spam messages.

raw.title: Raw
raw.description: The entire email message in RFC 2822 format, base64url-encoded. This is the raw email message to import into the mailbox.

deleted.title: Deleted
deleted.description: Mark the email as permanently deleted (not TRASH) and only visible in Google Vault to a Vault administrator. Only used for Google Workspace accounts.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

never_mark_spam.title: Never Mark Spam
never_mark_spam.description: Ignore the Gmail spam classifier decision and never mark this email as SPAM in the mailbox.

internal_date_source.title: InternalDateSource
internal_date_source.description: Source for Gmail's internal date of the message.

process_for_calendar.title: Process For Calendar
process_for_calendar.description: Process calendar invites in the email and add any extracted meetings to the Google Calendar for this user.

gmail.name: Insert message into mailbox
gmail.description: Tool to insert a message into the user's mailbox similar to IMAP APPEND. Use when you need to add an email directly to a mailbox bypassing most scanning and classification. This does not send a message.

raw.title: Raw
raw.description: The entire email message in RFC 2822 formatted and base64url encoded string. This is the raw message content that will be inserted into the mailbox.

deleted.title: Deleted
deleted.description: Mark the email as permanently deleted (not TRASH) and only visible in Google Vault to a Vault administrator. Only used for Google Workspace accounts.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

internalDateSource.title: InternalDateSource
internalDateSource.description: Source for Gmail's internal date of the message.

gmail.name: List CSE identities
gmail.description: Lists a page of client-side encrypted identities and their key-pair associations. A response indicating that CSE is not enabled is returned as an empty list.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The requester's primary email address. Use 'me' to indicate the authenticated user.

page_size.title: Page Size
page_size.description: The number of identities to return. If not provided, the page size will default to 20 entries.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Pagination token indicating which page of identities to return.

gmail.name: List CSE key pairs
gmail.description: Lists a page of client-side encryption key pairs, including public keys and enablement states. A response indicating that CSE is not enabled is returned as an empty list.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The requester's primary email address. Use 'me' to indicate the authenticated user.

page_size.title: Page Size
page_size.description: The number of key pairs to return per page. If not provided, the page size will default to 20 entries.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Pagination token indicating which page of key pairs to return. Omit to return the first page.

gmail.name: List Drafts
gmail.description: Retrieves a paginated list of email drafts from a user's Gmail account. Use verbose=true to get full draft details including subject, body, sender, and timestamp. Draft ordering is non-guaranteed; iterate using page_token until it is absent to retrieve all drafts. Newly created drafts may not appear immediately. Rapid calls may trigger 403 userRateLimitExceeded or 429 errors; apply exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) before retrying.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: User's mailbox ID; use 'me' for the authenticated user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own mailbox.

verbose.title: Verbose
verbose.description: If true, fetches full draft details including subject, sender, recipient, body, and timestamp. If false, returns only draft IDs (faster). Increases response payload size; tune max_results accordingly. Use verbose=true before destructive operations to confirm draft identity by subject, recipient, and timestamp.
verbose.human_parameter_description: Decide if you want detailed information about each draft or just the basic IDs. More details can help you see what’s inside.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Token from a previous response to retrieve a specific page of drafts. Ordering is non-guaranteed; continue paginating until page_token is absent in the response to retrieve all drafts.
page_token.human_parameter_description: Use this token to get the next page of draft results if you have more drafts to display.

max_results.title: Max Results
max_results.description: Maximum number of drafts to return per page.
max_results.human_parameter_description: Specify how many drafts you want to retrieve in one request. Choose between 1 and 500.

gmail.name: List Gmail filters
gmail.description: Tool to list all Gmail filters (rules) in the mailbox. Use for security audits to detect malicious filter rules or before creating new filters to avoid duplicates.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address or the special value 'me' to indicate the authenticated user whose filters will be retrieved.

gmail.name: List forwarding addresses
gmail.description: Tool to list all forwarding addresses for the specified Gmail account. Use when you need to retrieve the email addresses that are allowed to be used for forwarding messages.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address or the special value 'me' to indicate the authenticated user whose forwarding addresses will be retrieved.

gmail.name: List Gmail history
gmail.description: Lists Gmail mailbox change history since a known history ID for incremental sync, with optional label and history-type filters and pagination. An empty history list means no records matched the request, not necessarily that no mailbox changes occurred.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address. Use 'me' to specify the authenticated user.
user_id.human_parameter_description: The email address or identifier of the user whose mailbox you want to access. Use 'me' to access your own mailbox.

label_id.title: Label Id
label_id.description: Only return history records involving messages with this label ID.
label_id.human_parameter_description: Filter records to include only those related to a specific label. This helps you focus on changes that matter to you.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Token to retrieve a specific page of results. If the response includes nextPageToken, loop requests using this parameter until no nextPageToken is returned; failing to paginate will silently miss changes.
page_token.human_parameter_description: Use this token if you want to get a specific page of results. It helps in navigating through large sets of data.

max_results.title: Max Results
max_results.description: Maximum number of history records to return. Default is 100; max is 500.
max_results.human_parameter_description: Specify the maximum number of history records to fetch. This controls how much data you want to retrieve at one time.

history_types.title: History Types
history_types.description: Filter by specific history types. Allowed values: messageAdded, messageDeleted, labelAdded, labelRemoved.
history_types.human_parameter_description: Select the types of changes you want to retrieve, like added or deleted messages. This helps refine your search results.

start_history_id.title: Start History Id
start_history_id.description: Required. Returns history records after this ID. If the ID is invalid or too old, the API returns 404. Perform a full sync in that case. Should be a numeric string. On 404 (historyIdTooOld) or 400 (invalidArgument), recover by fetching a fresh historyId via GMAIL_GET_PROFILE, then perform a one-time full sync via GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS before resuming incremental calls.
start_history_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the unique history ID to start retrieving records. This helps in fetching changes made after a specific point.

gmail.name: List Gmail labels
gmail.description: Retrieves all system and user-created labels for a Gmail account in a single unpaginated response. Primary use: obtain internal label IDs (e.g., 'Label_123') required by other Gmail tools — display names cannot be used as label identifiers and cause silent failures or errors. System labels (INBOX, UNREAD, SPAM, TRASH, etc.) are case-sensitive and must be used exactly as returned; INBOX, SPAM, and TRASH are read-only and cannot be added/removed via label modification tools. The Gmail search 'label:' operator accepts display names, but label_ids parameters in tools like GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS require internal IDs from this tool — mixing conventions yields zero results silently. Do not hardcode label IDs across sessions; refresh via this tool on conflict errors.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: Identifies the Gmail account (owner's email or 'me' for authenticated user) for which labels will be listed.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the email address or identifier of the Gmail account whose labels you want to list. Use 'me' to access your own account.

include_details.title: Include Details
include_details.description: If true, fetches detailed info for each label including message/thread counts (messagesTotal, messagesUnread, threadsTotal, threadsUnread). This requires additional API calls and may be slower for accounts with many labels. If false (default), returns basic label info (id, name, type) which is faster. Counts are eventually consistent and may lag real-time mailbox state by a few seconds.
include_details.human_parameter_description: Set to true if you need message and thread counts for each label. Leave false for faster results with basic label info.

gmail.name: List Gmail messages (Deprecated)
gmail.description: DEPRECATED: Use GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS instead. Lists the messages in the user's mailbox. Use when you need to retrieve a list of email messages with optional filtering by labels or search query.

q.title: Q
q.description: Only return messages matching the specified query. Supports the same query format as the Gmail search box. For example, 'from:someuser@example.com is:unread'. Cannot be used when accessing the API using the gmail.metadata scope.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address or 'me' to specify the authenticated user.

label_ids.title: Label Ids
label_ids.description: Only return messages with labels that match all of the specified label IDs. Messages in a thread might have labels that other messages in the same thread don't have.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Page token to retrieve a specific page of results in the list.

max_results.title: Max Results
max_results.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. The maximum allowed value is 500.

include_spam_trash.title: Include Spam Trash
include_spam_trash.description: Include messages from SPAM and TRASH in the results. Default is false.

gmail.name: List send-as aliases
gmail.description: Lists the send-as aliases for a Gmail account, including the primary address and custom 'from' aliases. Use when you need to retrieve available sending addresses for composing emails.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address or the special value 'me' to indicate the authenticated user whose send-as aliases will be retrieved.

gmail.name: List S/MIME configs
gmail.description: Lists S/MIME certificate configurations for a specified Gmail send-as alias. If Gmail reports that the feature is not enabled, returns an empty list with S/MIME marked disabled.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

send_as_email.title: Send As Email
send_as_email.description: The email address that appears in the 'From:' header for mail sent using this alias.

gmail.name: List threads
gmail.description: Retrieves a list of email threads from a Gmail account, identified by `user_id` (email address or 'me'), supporting filtering and pagination. Spam and trash are excluded by default unless explicitly targeted via `label:spam` or `label:trash` in the query.

query.title: Query
query.description: Filter for threads, using Gmail search query syntax (e.g., 'from:user@example.com is:unread'). Supported operators include `from:`, `to:`, `subject:`, `label:`, `is:unread`, `has:attachment`, `after:`, `before:`. Dates must use `YYYY/MM/DD` format; date operators are UTC-based. Exact subject phrases require quotes (e.g., `subject:'meeting notes'`).
query.human_parameter_description: Use this field to search for specific threads based on criteria like sender or subject.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address or 'me' to specify the authenticated Gmail account.
user_id.human_parameter_description: Provide the email address or 'me' to refer to your own Gmail account.

verbose.title: Verbose
verbose.description: If false, returns threads with basic fields (id, snippet, historyId). If true, returns threads with complete message details including headers, body, attachments, and metadata for each message in the thread. Combining `verbose=true` with large `max_results` produces very large responses; keep `max_results` modest when verbose is enabled.
verbose.human_parameter_description: Choose whether you want just the basic thread info or detailed message content.

page_token.title: Page Token
page_token.description: Token from a previous response to retrieve a specific page of results; omit for the first page.
page_token.human_parameter_description: If you're looking for more threads, use this token to get the next set of results.

max_results.title: Max Results

recipient_email.description: Primary recipient's email address. Must be a valid email address (e.g., 'user@example.com') or display name format (e.g., 'John Doe <user@example.com>'). Optional - if not provided, previous recipients are preserved.

extra_recipients.title: Extra Recipients
extra_recipients.description: Additional 'To' recipients' email addresses. Each must be a valid email address or display name format. Should only be used if recipient_email is also provided.

include_signature.title: Include Signature
include_signature.description: Append the sender's Gmail signature (the 'Send mail as' signature configured in Gmail settings) to the message body, ahead of any quoted or forwarded content. Skipped when the body already ends with that signature, when no signature is configured, or when the connection lacks permission to read Gmail settings. Set to false to send the body exactly as provided.
include_signature.human_parameter_description: Append the sender's configured Gmail signature to the message.

gmail.name: Update IMAP settings
gmail.description: Tool to update IMAP settings for a Gmail account. Use when you need to modify IMAP configuration such as enabling/disabling IMAP, setting auto-expunge behavior, or configuring folder size limits.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether IMAP is enabled for the account.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

autoExpunge.title: Auto Expunge
autoExpunge.description: If this value is true, Gmail will immediately expunge a message when it is marked as deleted in IMAP. Otherwise, Gmail will wait for an update from the client before expunging messages marked as deleted.

maxFolderSize.title: Max Folder Size
maxFolderSize.description: An optional limit on the number of messages that an IMAP folder may contain. Legal values are 0, 1000, 2000, 5000 or 10000. A value of zero is interpreted to mean that there is no limit.

expungeBehavior.title: Expunge Behavior
expungeBehavior.description: The action that will be executed on a message when it is marked as deleted and expunged from the last visible IMAP folder. Possible values: 'expungeBehaviorUnspecified' (Unspecified behavior), 'archive' (Archive messages marked as deleted), 'trash' (Move messages marked as deleted to the trash), 'deleteForever' (Immediately and permanently delete messages marked as deleted).

gmail.name: Update Label
gmail.description: Updates an existing Gmail label's name, visibility settings, or color to help organize the mailbox. Color is available for user labels and requires both a background and text color from Gmail's supported palette.

input_parameters.title: UpdateLabelRequest

id.title: Id
id.description: The ID of the label to update.

name.title: Name
name.description: The display name of the label.

color.title: UpdateLabelColor

textColor.title: Text Color
textColor.description: The text color of the label, represented as hex string. This field is required in order to set the color of a label. Only predefined Gmail color values are allowed. See: https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/labels#color_palette

backgroundColor.title: Background Color
backgroundColor.description: The background color represented as hex string #RRGGBB (ex #000000). This field is required in order to set the color of a label. Only predefined Gmail color values are allowed. See: https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/labels#color_palette

color.description: Color settings for the label. Both backgroundColor and textColor must be provided together.

userId.title: User Id
userId.description: The user's email address. The special value `me` can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

labelListVisibility.title: LabelListVisibility
labelListVisibility.description: Visibility of the label in the label list (Gmail sidebar).

messageListVisibility.title: MessageListVisibility
messageListVisibility.description: Visibility of messages with this label in the message list.

input_parameters.description: Request model for updating a Gmail label.

gmail.name: Update Language Settings
gmail.description: Tool to update the language settings for a Gmail user. Use when you need to change the display language preference for the authenticated user or a specific Gmail account. The returned displayLanguage may differ from the requested value if Gmail selects a close variant.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The email address of the Gmail user whose language settings are to be updated, or the special value 'me' to indicate the currently authenticated user.

display_language.title: Display Language
display_language.description: The language to display Gmail in, formatted as an RFC 3066 Language Tag (e.g., 'en-GB' for British English, 'fr' for French, 'ja' for Japanese, 'es' for Spanish, 'de' for German, 'en' for English). The set of languages supported by Gmail evolves over time. Note: Gmail may save a close variant if the requested language is not directly supported. For example, if you request a regional variant that's not available, Gmail may save the base language instead.

gmail.name: Update POP settings
gmail.description: Tool to update POP settings for a Gmail account. Use when you need to configure POP access window or message disposition behavior.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

disposition.title: Disposition
disposition.description: The action that will be executed on a message after it has been fetched via POP.

access_window.title: AccessWindow
access_window.description: The range of messages which are accessible via POP.

gmail.name: Update send-as alias
gmail.description: Updates a Gmail send-as alias, including its display name, signature, reply-to address, or SMTP settings; Gmail sanitizes HTML signatures before saving. The tool declares support for service-account OAuth, not standard OAuth; non-primary addresses require domain-wide delegation.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: The email address of the Gmail user whose send-as alias to update, or the special value 'me' to indicate the authenticated user.

smtp_msa.title: SmtpMsa

host.title: Host
host.description: The hostname of the SMTP service. Required when configuring SMTP.

port.title: Port
port.description: The port of the SMTP service. Required when configuring SMTP.

password.title: Password
password.description: SMTP authentication password. Write-only field, never appears in responses.

username.title: Username
username.description: SMTP authentication username. Write-only field, never appears in responses.

securityMode.title: Security Mode
securityMode.description: Protocol for securing SMTP communication. Required when configuring SMTP.

smtp_msa.description: SMTP relay configuration for the send-as alias.

signature.title: Signature
signature.description: Optional HTML signature for messages composed with this alias in Gmail web UI. Gmail sanitizes HTML before saving. Only added to new emails.

is_default.title: Is Default
is_default.description: Set to true to make this the default 'From:' address for composing messages and vacation auto-replies. Setting true makes the previous default false. Only legal writable value is true.

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: Name to appear in 'From:' header. For custom from addresses, Gmail populates with primary account name if empty. Admin restrictions may silently fail updates to primary login name.

send_as_email.title: Send As Email
send_as_email.description: The send-as alias email address to update. This is the email address that appears in the 'From:' header.

treat_as_alias.title: Treat As Alias
treat_as_alias.description: Whether Gmail treats this address as an alias for the user's primary email. Only applies to custom from aliases.

reply_to_address.title: Reply To Address
reply_to_address.description: Optional email address for 'Reply-To:' header. Gmail omits header if empty.

gmail.name: Update Vacation Settings
gmail.description: Tool to update vacation responder settings for a Gmail user. Use when you need to configure out-of-office auto-replies.

userId.title: User Id
userId.description: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

endTime.title: End Time
endTime.description: An optional end time for sending auto-replies (epoch ms). When this is specified, Gmail will automatically reply only to messages that it receives before the end time. If both startTime and endTime are specified, startTime must precede endTime.

startTime.title: Start Time
startTime.description: An optional start time for sending auto-replies (epoch ms). When this is specified, Gmail will automatically reply only to messages that it receives after the start time. If both startTime and endTime are specified, startTime must precede endTime.

enableAutoReply.title: Enable Auto Reply
enableAutoReply.description: Flag that controls whether Gmail automatically replies to messages.

responseSubject.title: Response Subject
responseSubject.description: Optional text to prepend to the subject line in vacation responses. In order to enable auto-replies, either the response subject or the response body must be nonempty.

responseBodyHtml.title: Response Body Html
responseBodyHtml.description: Response body in HTML format. Gmail will sanitize the HTML before storing it. If both response_body_plain_text and response_body_html are specified, response_body_html will be used.

restrictToDomain.title: Restrict To Domain
restrictToDomain.description: Flag that determines whether responses are sent to recipients who are outside of the user's domain. This feature is only available for Google Workspace users.

restrictToContacts.title: Restrict To Contacts
restrictToContacts.description: Flag that determines whether responses are sent to recipients who are not in the user's list of contacts.

responseBodyPlainText.title: Response Body Plain Text
responseBodyPlainText.description: Response body in plain text format. If both response_body_plain_text and response_body_html are specified, response_body_html will be used.

gmail.name: Who Am I
gmail.description: Return the identity (email, name) of the connected Gmail account.

input_parameters.title: GmailWhoAmIRequest
input_parameters.description: Strict request contract for the Gmail identity action.
